descriptionChirho: Adverb functioning as a restrictive particle meaning 'exclusively, nothing more than, merely.' This is the dominant usage (65 of 67 occurrences). Multilingual translations consistently use restrictive-exclusive terms: spa 'solo/solamente,' hin 'keval/sirf,' arb 'faqat,' kor 'danji/ojik,' swa 'tu.' Used to limit scope: 'not only... but also' (ou monon... alla kai), 'only believe' (monon pisteue). The Arabic 'faqat' is an exclusively restrictive particle with no overlap with the solitary/companionship domain, confirming this as a discrete lexical sense.

Adverb indicating a state of being unaccompanied or solitary, describing isolation or lack of companions rather than restriction. Occurs twice. Multilingual evidence clearly distinguishes this from the restrictive sense: hin 'akele' (solitary, vs 'keval' restrictive), arb 'wahdahu' (by oneself, vs 'faqat' only), swa 'peke yake' (by oneself). The Arabic 'wahdahu' specifically denotes being alone/by oneself and is never used as a restrictive particle. Korean 'hollo/honja' (alone) likewise differs from 'danji' (merely). This solitary-state meaning belongs to a different semantic domain (companionship/isolation) than the restrictive-exclusive sense.
